title: 20210506-sentencing-process-report-on-public-consultation-exercise-final.pdf — section 12
text:
25. The word “physical” has been removed from the guideline’s explanation of harm.
This is intended to make it clear that harm includes, but is not limited to , physical
harm, and covers other forms of harm. Greater emphasis has also been given to
the impact that an offence has on any victim, including a list of examples of the sort
of factors which might bear on the assessment of harm.
“Double-counting”
Question 2

26. Question 2 asked whether the guideline’s approach to avoiding “double -counting”
is appropriate.

27. By “double-counting” the Council means that, when a factor is taken into account in
the assessment of seriousness, it should not thereafter also be treated as
aggravating or mitigating the sentence at step 3 in the sentencing process.

28. Although respondents generally supported the guideline’s treatment of this issue ,
some suggested that the guideline was not sufficiently clear about this – for
example, the term “double-counting” does not itself appear in the draft guideline.
What does the Council intend to do?
